clue.text: Earlier editions include remedies for lumbago

definitions.meaning: old issues of a magazine or newspaper, kept after newer ones come out
read whimsically: things that deaden pain in the lower back

explanation.definitionFit: Past issues of a periodical are called this; whimsically, painkillers for a sore lower back would also earn the name.

clue.text: Choice of headgear can cause a bitter argument

indicators.note: an argument is a row or dispute, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Picking a hat leads to a bitter quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'argument' signals the anagram of A BITTER; 'can cause' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cap worn by Catholic clergy is one item of headgear a person might select.

clue.text: Boxer causes scare!

indicators.note: the word scare is made into something else, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter in the ring gives everyone a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' is not a fighter but someone who puts goods into cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A packer who puts things into crates or boxes could be called this.

clue.text: Names a person from Minnesota

indicators.note: the answer is formed from the state name, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a US state is being identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals that the letters of MINNESOTA are rearranged; 'a person' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward people as candidates is to propose them by name.

clue.text: Grind which causes many to get sick

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so a large number
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A tedious grind that leaves lots of people unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinder for corn or pepper is this machine; also a verb meaning to crush to powder.

clue.text: Object to the inclusion of expensive quarter, but this increased affection

indicators.note: the first word takes the following pieces inside it

parts.note: an object or aim is an end
expensive means dear
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A protest against including a pricey district, which nonetheless made people fonder.
explanation.definitionFit: If something made others more fond of you, it won their love and warmed them to you.

clue.text: Hits with footwear!

definitions.meaning: garments worn on the feet inside shoes

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for punches, and also the knitted garments worn on the feet.

clue.text: Continue to make a fuss

definitions.meaning: behave in an overexcited, complaining way

explanation.definitionFit: Means go on doing something, and is also British slang for a commotion or behaving fussily.

clue.text: There's a dreadfully poor rate for his job!

definitions.text: There's a dreadfully poor rate for his job!

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something badly done, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about low pay for someone's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard worker or machine worker is a person whose job, the clue grumbles, pays badly.

clue.text: Looked as though the engineers got a point, but the doctor won

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a medical degree
won means was ahead, led

explanation.surface: An engineering team scores, but the medic comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To have looked like something is to have appeared similar to it.

clue.text: Skip the sauce

definitions.meaning: a pickled flower bud used in a sauce for fish or mutton

explanation.definitionFit: A playful leap, and the pickled bud that flavours a classic sauce.

clue.text: Wearing an article of jewellery after getting it back

indicators.note: the jewellery piece goes after the turned word
the word it is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: Putting on a piece of jewellery once it has been returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting it back' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wearing is exhausting, sapping one's energy.

clue.text: One who goes near might spy bears

indicators.note: might hints at what the words could become if rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone approaching may catch sight of bears.
explanation.definitionFit: A person walking past is someone who happens to go close by.

clue.text: Some sort of total-about 100-for US authoress

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes round the number
sort of means a version of, so the word total is rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Something like a total of roughly a hundred, for an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' is a link; ALOTT, the anagram of TOTAL, is placed round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May, author of Little Women, was an American novelist.

clue.text: Husband in a jam

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to use sparingly and save

explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to save them; also a whole-fruit preserve like jam.

clue.text: Eli turns around to produce an effect

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the two words are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Eli spins around to create an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'an effect' read as part of the surface; the definition is 'produce', in the sense of lead to.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead to an outcome or cause it is to bring it about.

clue.text: The very last place to find superlative talk

parts.note: to utter is to say or talk
most forms the superlative of many adjectives

explanation.surface: The final spot where you'll hear the best conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place to find' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Means extreme or farthest, so the very last or furthest of all.

clue.text: This usually produces a response

parts.note: in church services a short sentence said by the priest is answered by the congregation

explanation.definitionFit: A short line said by a minister in liturgy, which the congregation answers.

clue.text: In showing relative around, found something very nasty

indicators.note: the relative goes round the little word

parts.note: a sister is a family relative

explanation.surface: Discovering something horrid when showing a family member about.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening or menacing, suggesting evil, is extremely unpleasant.

clue.text: He's a cold fellow and won't last long

definitions.text: He's a cold fellow and won't last long

parts.words: He's a cold fellow and won't last long
parts.note: seems to describe an aloof, ailing man, but means a figure built in winter that melts

explanation.definitionFit: A figure built from packed winter flakes is chilly and melts away in a thaw.

clue.text: Begins with jumps

explanation.definitionFit: Means commences, and also sudden flinches of fright.

clue.text: Ran round the edge, and fell over

indicators.note: the word for ran goes round the edge

parts.note: to have run fast is to have sped
a lip is the rim or edge of something

explanation.surface: Someone running around a rim takes a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose footing and fall is to stumble down.

clue.text: It's not a bright outlook, being in charge of a group of actors!

parts.note: over means above in authority
the cast is the company of players in a show

explanation.surface: A director running a troupe faces gloomy prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudy, grey sky gives a dull view of the weather.

clue.text: Prices lettuce on a back street

parts.note: cos is a long-leaved lettuce, called romaine in the US

indicators.note: the abbreviation for street is turned round

explanation.surface: Lettuce prices on a backstreet market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts charged for goods are what they demand in money.

clue.text: Bad start to early letter I sent to sultanate

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a rune is a character of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A poor opening to an old letter mailed to an Eastern kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: A small state on Borneo ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Dress while still in bed

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Dress while still in bed (3,2)'. 'still in bed' defines it and 'Dress' gives PUT ON read backwards, but no word signals the reversal; the clue may be cut short.

clue.text: Spur geese into action partly by encouragement

definitions.text: Spur geese into action partly by encouragement

indicators.note: only part of the two words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Driving a flock of geese along with coaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To push or press someone on with encouragement is to goad them forward.

clue.text: Girl who, but for the French, might have taken Civic Centre

indicators.note: the French word would take the central letter inside it

parts.note: mais is French for but

indicators.note: the centre of the five-letter word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A young woman who, without the French, might have occupied the town hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Fish is about right for chap with redhead

indicators.note: the fish wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
Otto is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A fish is just right for a red-haired man.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokey nickname for a person with ginger hair, likened to the orange vegetable.

clue.text: Poetic animal takes very odd poetry, but in the style to be expected

definitions.text: in the style to be expected

indicators.note: the horse takes the rearranged verse inside it

parts.note: steed is a literary word for a horse

indicators.note: very odd means bizarre, so the letters of poetry are jumbled

explanation.surface: A horse in verse handles strange poems, yet all quite conventionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Conforming to a fixed, conventional image is predictable and formulaic.
